blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Character Error Rate (CER), the standard metric for OCR and vision-language models (VLMs), charges a typo as much as a wrong name. We introduce semCER, which keeps CER's alignment and denominator and charges each grapheme edit a severity from an LLM judge, with no word segmentation. Normalized CER keeps the score of a whole transcription, where it tracks readers as well as semCER or better, and semCER breaks that score down into named edits. The charges track readers' ratings edit by edit in English, Vietnamese, and Chinese and put the edits readers rate most severe near the top of a sorted list. On pairs drawn where CER and semCER disagreed, readers side with semCER more often than with normalized CER in English and Chinese, and equally often in Vietnamese. Across 16 languages, the judge charges a wrong diacritic or tone mark almost nothing in Spanish but nearly a wrong letter's severity in Telugu. Where we can count real words, a general VLM's wrong letter forms one far above chance while a classical pipeline's stays near it. We release the 61 million judged edits, the aggregated reader ratings, and the distilled scorer at https://github.com/nguyenx2t/semcer.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Consider two optical character recognition (OCR) systems that each make one error on an English line ( Equal CER , Unequal Damage: Severity-Weighted Character Error Rate for OCR ). One writes strategically as strategicallv , and the other misreads the agency acronym AGFD as ACFD . A reader fixes the first without hesitation but cannot fix the second, which silently renames an organization. Yet Character Error Rate ( CER ), the standard metric for OCR and vision–language models (VLMs) alike Ouyang et al. (2025) ; Neudecker et al. (2021) ; Beyene and Dancy (2026) , charges the two the same, because it counts edits and divides by the reference length, whatever each edit costs the reader.
blocks.zh: 考虑两个光学字符识别(OCR)系统,每个系统都会在一条英语线上发生一个错误(等于CER, Unequal Damage:Severity-Wighted Chart Error rate for OCR ). 另一则将机构缩写为ACFD。 一个读者毫不犹豫地修补第一个,但不能修补第二个,后者默默地重新命名一个组织. 然而字符错误率(CER),即OCR和视觉语言模型的标准度量标准(VLMs),如欧阳等人(2025年);Neudecker等人(2021年);Beyene和Dancy(2026年),对两者收取相同的费用,因为它按参考长度计算编辑和划分,无论每次编辑花费读者多少。

blocks.en: Benchmarks and scoring toolkits soften the uniform charge by removing or folding whitespace, case, and punctuation before counting Ouyang et al. (2025) ; Yang et al. (2025) ; Vaessen (2025) , but normalization still charges every surviving edit alike. In Equal CER , Unequal Damage: Severity-Weighted Character Error Rate for OCR , two Vietnamese lines contain the same substitution, ấ → \to á. Readers rate the first recoverable from its sentence and the second unrecoverable because it changes the heroine’s name, while normalization charges both the same. VLMs add a failure mode of their own, since they decode through a strong language prior and write fluent wrong words Gardella et al. (2026) ; Karamolegkou et al. (2026) ; Liang et al. (2026) ; Lee et al. (2026) that CER charges no more than a typo.
blocks.zh: 基准和评分工具包在计算欧阳等人(2025年)、杨等人(2025年)、瓦森(2025年)之前, 在等效CER中,不均匀损害:OCR的Severity-Wighted字符错误率,两条越南行包含相同的替换, car →\to á. 读者从句子中评分第一笔可收回,第二笔不可收回,因为它改变了女主角的名字,而正常化既收取同样的费用。 VLMs增加了自己的故障模式,因为它们在Gardella et al.(2026)之前通过强语言解码并写出流利的错误词;Karamolegkou et al.(2026),Liang et al.(2026),Lee et al.(2026),CER收费不超过打字费.

blocks.en: Metrics that do weigh meaning either rate the whole output, as semantic similarity scores and most LLM judges do, or grade spans marked outside CER ’s alignment, as MQM does ( Freitag et al., 2021 ) . Neither stays on CER ’s scale. A rate that keeps CER ’s form and changes its charge raises three questions. (Q1) Which unit do we charge when a script puts no spaces between words? (Q2) Are a few severity classes fine enough to choose between two transcriptions that both read almost right? (Q3) Where does a severity still help once a benchmark has normalized cosmetic edits away?
blocks.zh: 量子的量子,如果不是像语义相似的分数和大多数LLM评委那样对全部输出进行评分,就是像MQM那样在CER对齐之外标出分数(Freitag等人,2021年)。 也不停留在CER的规模上。 保持CER形式并改变其收费的费率引起了三个问题。 (问题1)当一个脚本没有文字间空格时,我们收取哪个单位? (问题2) 几门重度课是否足够精细, 可以在两个都读对的抄本中选择? (问题3)一旦一个基准将化妆品编辑正常化,那么严重程度还能有什么帮助?

blocks.en: In this paper, we introduce semCER , which answers Q1 by design. It charges the grapheme clusters that CER ’s alignment already produces and keeps CER ’s denominator. One definition therefore applies to alphabets, abugidas, abjads, and unspaced scripts without word segmentation, and charging every edit one gives back CER exactly. For Q2, a judge rates each edit on a five-level rubric, and semCER reads the charge from the judge’s probabilities rather than its most likely level, so two edits at the same level can still differ. Whether that finer charge agrees with readers and chooses between two almost-right transcriptions better than a three-class charge does (Q2), and whether it adds to normalization (Q3), are empirical questions. We answer them by testing semCER against readers, a three-class charge, and normalized CER . The answers make semCER a tool for finding and grading errors, while normalized CER remains the score for a whole transcription. We make four contributions. • semCER orders the errors to check. Sorted by charge, the edits readers rate most severe come near the top, an order CER cannot give. The charge tracks readers’ ratings beyond what the edit’s type predicts, and in English and Chinese beyond whether normalization would remove the edit ( Section 5 ). • Readers mostly side with semCER where it disagrees with CER . On pairs drawn where CER and semCER ranked two transcriptions in opposite order, readers of English and Chinese side with semCER on 71 71 and 78 % 78\% of pairs. They side with normalized CER , the stronger baseline, on 58 58 and 60 % 60\% , and Vietnamese readers side with the two equally often. On the same pairs, readers of all three languages side with semCER significantly more often than with a three-class charge ( Section 6 ). • An equal edit count hides unequal damage, set by the language and by the system. The judge’s charge for an edit varies across 16 16 languages with the price of the smallest edit, which costs almost nothing in Spanish and nearly a wrong letter’s severity in Telugu. Where a general VLM and EasyOCR tie on edit count, the VLM’s edits cost more in Chinese and Vietnamese and less in English, French, and Spanish. The split follows the price of the smallest edit, and at least three of the four VLMs show it in each language. The VLM’s letter errors cost more than a classical pipeline’s in every language where we can measure both, except Spanish, and they form real words where the pipeline’s form non-words, so a word-list check misses them ( Section 7 ). • A distilled scorer with fixed weights reproduces the judge. A 0.8 0.8 B student trained on the judge’s distributions, with no human rating, comes within 0.03 0.03 of the judge’s agreement with readers and orders nine in ten clear edit pairs as the judge does ( Section 8 ). We release it with the 61 61 million judged edits and the aggregated per-item reader ratings.

blocks.en:
Speech recognition has several error rates that keep
the word error rate’s form and replace its unit charge. EmbER discounts substitutions with similar word embeddings ( Bañeras Roux et al., 2022 ) , Semantic-WER weights entities and sentiment words ( Roy, 2021 ) , and SWWER weights words by BERT-derived importance ( Zhang and Ai, 2024 ) . Three others grade each error by its effect, minED ( Bañeras-Roux et al., 2024 ) , clinicians’ impact labels ( Ellis et al., 2026 ) , and the NER accuracy rate for live subtitling ( Romero-Fresco and Martínez Pérez, 2015 ) .

BERTScore, BLEURT, SemDist, and H_eval
compare the whole reference and hypothesis through embeddings or learned
scores ( Zhang et al., 2020 ; Sellam et al., 2020 ; Kim et al., 2021 ; Sasindran et al., 2023 ) , and aligned variants score token or
segment pairs ( Rugayan et al., 2022 ; Sasindran et al., 2024 ) . They charge a similarity on a scale
unrelated to CER ’s, and BERTScore responds weakly to small errors in lexically close candidates,
including a changed figure ( Hanna and Bojar, 2021 ; Huang et al., 2025 ) , which are the errors OCR makes.

blocks.en:
MQM annotates error spans by type and weights them by
severity ( Lommel et al., 2014 ; Freitag et al., 2021 ) , and GEMBA-MQM, AutoMQM, xCOMET, and TIGERScore have a
model mark and grade the spans ( Kocmi and Federmann, 2023 ; Fernandes et al., 2023 ; Guerreiro et al., 2024 ; Jiang et al., 2024 ) . In
grammatical error correction, CLEME2.0 also weights individual edits with a language model ( Ye et al., 2025 ) . It aligns the
erroneous source, the system’s correction, and the reference corrections into word chunks and scores
each chunk as a hit, a wrong, a missing, or an unnecessary correction. It then weights a chunk by embedding
similarity or by an LLM’s rating of how important the correction is and combines the four scores
with fitted coefficients. JELV and LLM judges likewise rate a correction from its marked
edits ( Zhan et al., 2026 ; Kobayashi et al., 2024 ) . semCER has only a reference and no erroneous source text, so it scores
the recoverability of each error in the transcription, where CLEME2.0 scores the importance of each correction.
It charges the graphemes of a fixed unit-cost alignment, which needs no word segmentation, and keeps CER ’s denominator, so charging every edit one gives CER back.

blocks.en:
OCR benchmarks transform text differently before
scoring ( Ouyang et al., 2025 ; Yang et al., 2025 ; Rice and Nartker, 1996 ) , and in speech the choice is known to distort
evaluation, since Whisper’s normalizer strips Indic vowel signs and flatters the
model ( Manohar and Pillai, 2024 ; Thennal et al., 2025 ) . A second line of work replaces the uniform
Levenshtein costs ( Levenshtein, 1966 ) with learned or tuned ones, either a weight per operation or
character pair that is fitted once and reused ( Ristad and Yianilos, 1998 ; Oncina and Sebban, 2006 ; Stanchev et al., 2019 ) or operation
probabilities from learned encodings of both strings ( Libovický and Fraser, 2022 ) . Normalization rewrites the
strings before alignment, and cost tables let the costs choose the alignment. semCER instead fixes a
unit-cost alignment first and charges its edits afterward.

blocks.en:
Other OCR metrics decompose page-level
error by pipeline stage ( Bourne et al., 2026 ) , ignore reading order ( Clausner et al., 2020 ) , or score
reconstruction fidelity against the page image ( Vandepitte, 2026 ) . SCORE, for generative parsing, adjusts the edit distance for representational variation and counts hallucinated and omitted tokens ( Li et al., 2025 ) . It normalizes the variation away before counting, while semCER charges
what survives. Unit-test benchmarks replace the edit count with binary checks per
page ( Poznanski et al., 2025 ) .

blocks.en: semCER has two parts, a definition that puts a severity in place of CER ’s unit charge and a judge that supplies the severity.

blocks.en: 3.1 Definition
blocks.zh: 3.1 定义

blocks.en: semCER replaces each edit’s unit charge in CER with a severity, so the first choice is what counts as one edit. Like CER , it charges characters rather than words, because a script with no spaces between words yields a word error rate only after a segmentation step whose mistakes the score inherits ( Thennal et al., 2025 ) (Q1). We treat a character in both scores as an extended grapheme cluster, following Unicode Standard Annex #29 ( Unicode Consortium, 2026 ) under Normalization Form C, so a base letter with its accents or tone marks is one unit, as grapheme-level OCR metrics recommend ( Nisfer et al., 2026 ) . Published CER implementations often count code points instead ( Vaessen, 2025 ) , which splits a syllable of an abugida into its consonant and vowel signs and counts an accented letter as one unit or several depending on how the text was encoded. Extended grapheme clusters approximate the characters a reader perceives and give the same units whatever the encoding form, so the judge rates one kind of unit in every language. We compute every CER in this work over the same grapheme clusters, case- and whitespace-sensitive, and call it unnormalized CER .

blocks.en: Each edit’s severity comes from a large language model judge, DeepSeek-V4-Flash Preview ( DeepSeek-AI, 2026 ) . It reads the full reference and output with the target edit marked in context ( Section A.1 ). It then rates how far the edit stops a reader from noticing and repairing it on the ordinal rubric of Table 1 , from 0 0 for a surface change to 4 4 for an error that leaves no signal. We fit no parameter to human ratings.

blocks.en: We compare the severity with three charges that use no judge, a table built from the judge’s corpus, and two coarser readouts of the same judge. The judge-free charges are CER ’s own per-edit charge, the filter label , and the real-word label . The filter label records whether an edit survives the character filter that OCR benchmarks apply before scoring, which keeps letters and digits and drops whitespace, punctuation, and symbols ( Ouyang et al., 2025 ) , and the real-word label whether the edit forms a real word. The type table charges an edit the corpus-mean severity of its type and reads the judge’s corpus but not the line. The coarser readouts are the class charge , the judge’s most likely level charged on three fixed class weights, and the whole-line judgment , one rating of the whole line. Normalized CER applies the filter and folds case before alignment.

blocks.en: A user who checks a transcription wants to know which errors to look at first, and a score alone does not say. semCER also orders the edits behind its score, so we first test that order against readers and then ask what the severity adds to the simpler charges an order could use.

blocks.en: 9 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 9 结论

blocks.en: CER counts edits, and normalization decides which edits to count, but neither says what an edit costs the reader. We introduced semCER , which charges each grapheme edit a judged severity, without word segmentation, and keeps CER ’s alignment and denominator. The two scores divide the work. Normalized CER tracks readers’ ratings of whole transcriptions as well as semCER or better, so it remains the score for a transcription. An equal edit count is a tie for CER , and semCER breaks it with charges that follow the language’s smallest edit and the system’s kind of error. Where the two scores order a pair of transcriptions the other way, readers of English and Chinese mostly side with semCER . They do so most of all where normalization leaves CER ’s choice in place, and readers of all three languages side with semCER over a three-class charge. The score is a sum over the aligned edits, so each decision between two transcriptions breaks down into named edits and their charges. Those charges track readers’ ratings edit by edit in three languages and put the errors readers rate most severe near the top of a sorted list. We therefore recommend normalized CER for scoring a transcription. Beside it, semCER , computed locally with the distilled scorer, chooses between transcriptions where CER ties or the two scores disagree, and names the edits behind the choice.

blocks.en: Holm correction ( Holm, 1979 ) runs within four kinds of family. 1. In the preference test, each comparison on each set of pairs forms a family of its three languages, for semCER ’s margins and for those scored with the judge’s earlier severities, the distilled scorer, and the second judge ( Figs. 7 and 9 ). 2. On the pair-level pool, the contrasts with semCER form one family per language ( Table 7 ). The class charge lies outside it, since we added it after that test, so its row carries an uncorrected interval. 3. The 24 24 equal-count contrasts form one family ( Table 10 ). 4. Each comparison of the severity-sorted list with a baseline forms a family of its three languages, on the top-of-list share for the best judge-free order and the type table and on the top 10 % 10\% for CER ’s charge ( Table 6 ). We compute each partial correlation on ranks after regressing both the score and the readers’ mean rating on the sampling band and the named baseline. The single-edit partials given the band alone and given the type table, the filter label, or both carry no Holm correction, since each answers a pre-specified question. blocks.en: A pair is a near miss when its higher- CER output meets three conditions, which we defined from an earlier reading of the same pool.
